status: starting values for the first sample; the workshop sets the final numbers

sources.coat: Kennel Club / FCI standard: coat short, close and smooth, fine in texture (facts extracted, text not copied)
sources.head_skin: Kennel Club standard: head skin slightly loose and finely wrinkled without excess; an over-nose wrinkle must not hide the eyes or nose
sources.tail: Kennel Club standard: tail short, thick at the root, tapering, set low, carried down
sources.colour: Kennel Club standard: brindle, red, fawn, white and pied; colours read from the customer's photos via the photo-textured 3D model

stock_fur: white acrylic pile on knitted polyester backing, short, dense and smooth (not shaggy), pile at least 8 mm so the longest zone can be trimmed to length

trim_zones.note: shortest, velvety: jowls, muzzle tops, chin
short and smooth so the wrinkles read; ears both sides
standard coat; brushed back and down
same as the body: a bulldog has no ruff

size_rule: fur lengths scale with plush size; at 350 mm every leg is already wider than the 25 mm tube minimum (27.6 mm), so the bulldog keeps its true proportions; only the tail stub is set at the minimum (30 mm wide)
markings_rule: brindle and other markings are airbrushed on the white stock fur from the colour guide; where the dog has a crisp white edge (blaze, bib, socks) the nearest seam can be moved onto that edge so the colour change hides it (craftsman approval per seam)
wrinkle_rule: the 3D shape stays smooth; wrinkles are needle-sculpted from the wrinkle map and shaded darker in the crease with the airbrush (competitor reviews ask for deeper, darker head wrinkles)
